===== src/Triggers.js =====
/**
 * UCBAC Stats — Triggers.gs
 *
 * Keeps the derived layer current without anyone remembering to rebuild it.
 *
 * Rosters change at unpredictable intervals for weeks at a time, so nothing here
 * assumes a starting point or a finished state. Edits mark the database dirty; a
 * short-interval trigger notices and rebuilds. A nightly pass rebuilds
 * unconditionally so a dropped flag can never leave the site stale for long.
 *
 * Run installTriggers() once. It is idempotent — it removes this project's
 * existing triggers before installing, so running it twice is harmless.
 */

const TRG = {
  DIRTY_KEY: 'UCBAC_DIRTY',
  LAST_BUILD_KEY: 'UCBAC_LAST_BUILD',
  LAST_ERROR_KEY: 'UCBAC_LAST_ERROR',
  SWEEP_MINUTES: 15,
  NIGHTLY_HOUR: 3,
  // Mail is checked on its own schedule, not the rebuild's. A player's
  // correction request marks nothing dirty, so a sweep that only runs when the
  // database changed would leave his coach unmailed until somebody edited a
  // roster.
  MAIL_MINUTES: 5
};

function props_() { return PropertiesService.getScriptProperties(); }

/**
 * Mark the database as needing a rebuild. Called from every write path.
 * `scope` is a comma-joined set so a burst of edits collapses into one rebuild.
 */
function markDirty_(scope) {
  if (typeof appPublicMarkEdit_ === 'function') appPublicMarkEdit_();
  const p = props_();
  const cur = String(p.getProperty(TRG.DIRTY_KEY) || '');
  const set = {};
  cur.split(',').forEach(function (s_) { if (s_) set[s_] = true; });
  (scope || 'all').split(',').forEach(function (s_) { if (s_) set[s_] = true; });
  p.setProperty(TRG.DIRTY_KEY, Object.keys(set).join(','));
}

function isDirty_() { return !!String(props_().getProperty(TRG.DIRTY_KEY) || ''); }
function clearDirty_() { props_().deleteProperty(TRG.DIRTY_KEY); }

/** Runs every SWEEP_MINUTES. Cheap when nothing changed. */
function sweepRebuild() {
  if (!isDirty_()) return 'clean — nothing to do';
  return runRebuild_('sweep');
}

/** Runs nightly regardless of the flag. */
function nightlyRebuild() { return runRebuild_('nightly'); }

/**
 * The one place a rebuild actually happens. Serialized, so a nightly pass and a
 * sweep firing together cannot interleave and half-write the derived tabs.
 */
function runRebuild_(reason) {
  const lock = LockService.getScriptLock();
  if (!lock.tryLock(5000)) return 'another rebuild is already running — skipped';
  const t0 = new Date().getTime();
  try {
    const appPublicBuild = typeof appPublicRebuildBegin_ === 'function' && appPublicRebuildBegin_();
    const log = [];
    log.push(rebuildDerived_());

    // A completed season's inputs no longer change, so the sweep only touches
    // the active one. A nightly or an explicit full pass does every season —
    // and the first run must, or the historical ballots never exist at all.
    const full = appPublicBuild || (reason === 'nightly' || reason === 'setup' || reason === 'manual');
    rowsOf_(CONFIG.TABS.SEASONS).forEach(function (s_) {
      const sid = String(s_.SeasonID).trim();
      const status = String(s_.Status || '').toUpperCase();
      if (full || sid === CONFIG.CURRENT_SEASON || status === 'ACTIVE') {
        log.push(rebuildAllConference_(sid));
      }
    });

    clearDirty_();
    /* The derived tabs now hold new numbers and the site is still serving the
       old ones, for up to fifteen minutes, from a cache that has no idea a
       rebuild happened. Somebody who enters Friday's scores and then looks at
       the standings sees last week's table and reasonably concludes the
       rebuild did not work. A rebuild that leaves the site showing the
       previous answer has not finished. */
    try { clearApiCache_(); } catch (ignore) {}
    const secs = ((new Date().getTime() - t0) / 1000).toFixed(1);
    const msg = '[' + reason + '] rebuilt in ' + secs + 's\n' + log.join('\n');
    props_().setProperty(TRG.LAST_BUILD_KEY, new Date().toISOString());
    props_().deleteProperty(TRG.LAST_ERROR_KEY);
    if (typeof appPublicRebuildFinish_ === 'function') appPublicRebuildFinish_(true);
    Logger.log(msg);
    return msg;
  } catch (e) {
    if (typeof appPublicRebuildFinish_ === 'function') appPublicRebuildFinish_(false);
    // leave the dirty flag set so the next sweep retries
    props_().setProperty(TRG.LAST_ERROR_KEY, new Date().toISOString() + '  ' + e.message);
    Logger.log('REBUILD FAILED (' + reason + '): ' + e.stack);
    throw e;
  } finally {
    lock.releaseLock();
  }
}

/**
 * Deliver whatever is queued in Notifications.
 *
 * Its own trigger, deliberately. sendPendingNotifications() has existed since
 * the account layer went in and nothing ever called it, so every approval
 * request, correction and decision since then has been written to the tab and
 * left there — the queue worked, the delivery was never scheduled, and the
 * symptom was silence rather than an error anybody could see.
 *
 * Never throws. A time trigger that throws mails the owner a stack trace on
 * every firing, which is a worse mailing problem than the one it reports.
 */
function deliverNotifications() {
  try {
    return sendPendingNotifications_();
  } catch (e) {
    Logger.log('deliverNotifications failed: ' + (e && e.message ? e.message : e));
    return 'failed: ' + (e && e.message ? e.message : e);
  }
}

/** Install the schedule. Safe to re-run. */
function installTriggers() {
  removeTriggers_();
  ScriptApp.newTrigger('sweepRebuild').timeBased()
    .everyMinutes(TRG.SWEEP_MINUTES).create();
  ScriptApp.newTrigger('nightlyRebuild').timeBased()
    .everyDays(1).atHour(TRG.NIGHTLY_HOUR).create();
  ScriptApp.newTrigger('deliverNotifications').timeBased()
    .everyMinutes(TRG.MAIL_MINUTES).create();
  const msg = 'Installed: sweepRebuild every ' + TRG.SWEEP_MINUTES +
              ' minutes, nightlyRebuild at ' + TRG.NIGHTLY_HOUR + ':00, ' +
              'deliverNotifications every ' + TRG.MAIL_MINUTES + ' minutes.';
  Logger.log(msg);
  return msg;
}

function removeTriggers_() {
  const all = ScriptApp.getProjectTriggers();
  var removed=0;
  all.forEach(function (t) {
    const fn = t.getHandlerFunction();
    /* Both spellings. A trigger installed while the handlers were briefly
       private is still out there under the underscored name, and clearing it
       is this function's job — otherwise reinstalling leaves a dead copy
       beside the live one. */
    if (['sweepRebuild', 'nightlyRebuild', 'deliverNotifications',
         'sweepRebuild_', 'nightlyRebuild_', 'deliverNotifications_'].indexOf(fn) >= 0) {
      ScriptApp.deleteTrigger(t); removed++;
    }
  });
  return 'Removed ' + removed + ' trigger(s).';
}

/** Operational status, for the admin view and for eyeballing in the editor. */
function buildStatus_() {
  const p = props_();
  const triggers = ScriptApp.getProjectTriggers()
    .filter(function (t) {
      return ["sweepRebuild", "nightlyRebuild"].indexOf(t.getHandlerFunction()) >= 0;
    })
    .map(function (t) { return t.getHandlerFunction(); });
  return {
    dirty: String(p.getProperty(TRG.DIRTY_KEY) || ''),
    lastBuild: p.getProperty(TRG.LAST_BUILD_KEY) || 'never',
    lastError: p.getProperty(TRG.LAST_ERROR_KEY) || '',
    triggersInstalled: triggers,
    sweepMinutes: TRG.SWEEP_MINUTES
  };
}

===== src/WebApps.js =====
/**
 * UCBAC Stats - WebApp.gs
 *
 * ONE deployment serves everything:
 *
 *   Deploy > New deployment > Web app
 *   Execute as: Me            Who has access: Anyone
 *
 * The public site needs no sign-in. The portal is the same URL with
 * ?page=portal, and its sign-in is an emailed one-time code (Auth.gs), so the
 * deployment never needs to run as the visitor. That matters twice over: a
 * deployment running as the visitor would ask every player to grant the
 * script's scopes to their own Google account, and would then read the
 * database AS that player, who has no access to the workbook and must never
 * be given any.
 *
 * After pasting new code, publish it: Deploy > Manage deployments > edit >
 * Version: New version. Saving files alone changes nothing anyone can see.
 *
 * Every svc* below is a pure pass-through carrying no logic of its own. They
 * are callable by anyone through google.script.run whatever the page chooses
 * to render, so authorization lives in the api* function and nowhere else;
 * hiding a control is never a control. Portal wrappers take the session token
 * as their FIRST argument and bind it for the request via withSession(); the
 * api* signatures underneath are unchanged.
 */

function doGet(e) {
  const page = String((e && e.parameter && e.parameter.page) || '').toLowerCase();
  if (page === 'policy') return policyPage_(e && e.parameter && e.parameter.doc);

  /* Every page load knows the deployment's real published address; the
     spreadsheet menu does not. Remember it here so a decision link built from
     the menu points somewhere a coach can actually open. */
  try { corrRememberBase_(); } catch (ignore) {}

  // an approve/reject link from a request email; the signature is the
  // authorization, checked inside apiDecideByLink / apiDecideCorrectionByLink
  const decide = String((e && e.parameter && e.parameter.decide) || '').toLowerCase();
  if (decide) {
    const corr = String((e && e.parameter && e.parameter.corr) || '');
    var out;
    try {
      // ?corr= is a stat correction from a coach's inbox; ?acc= an account request
      const r = corr ? apiDecideCorrectionByLink_(corr, decide, e.parameter.sig)
                     : apiDecideByLink_(e.parameter.acc, decide, e.parameter.sig);
      out = (r && r.message) || 'Done.';
      // a correction already settled is not an error, and says so itself
      if (corr && r && r.ok === false) out = (r && r.message) || 'Already decided.';
    } catch (err) {
      out = (err && err.message) || 'This link is not valid.';
    }
    const safe = String(out).replace(/[&<>"]/g, function (c) {
      return { '&': '&amp;', '<': '&lt;', '>': '&gt;', '"': '&quot;' }[c];
    });
    const home = String(ScriptApp.getService().getUrl() || '').split('?')[0];
    return HtmlService.createHtmlOutput(
      '<div style="font-family:system-ui,sans-serif;max-width:480px;margin:80px auto;' +
      'padding:24px;border:1px solid #ddd;border-radius:12px">' +
      '<h2 style="margin-top:0">UCBAC Stats</h2><p>' + safe + '</p>' +
      (corr ? '<p>The player has been told. Totals catch up within the hour.</p>' +
              '<p><a href="' + home + '?page=portal&view=signup">Create a coach account</a> ' +
              'to enter box scores and see these without waiting for an email.</p>' : '') +
      '<p><a href="' + home + '?page=portal">Open the portal</a></p></div>'
    ).setTitle('UCBAC Stats');
  }

  if (page === 'portal') {
    /* One tab, no frames. Google's sandbox will not render one Apps Script
       app inside another's iframe, so the portal is its own page again, but
       wearing the site's header, whose links navigate this same tab back to
       the public site. Sign-in returns to the site home, greeted by name. */
    const portal = HtmlService.createTemplateFromFile('Portal');
    portal.siteUrl = String(CONFIG.SITE_URL || '');
    portal.execUrl = String(ScriptApp.getService().getUrl() || '');
    /* ?view=signup opens on the Create an account form - the site's "Create
       a player account" button lands here. Anything else opens as usual. */
    portal.view = String((e && e.parameter && e.parameter.view) || '').replace(/[^a-z]/gi, '').toLowerCase();
    return portal
      .evaluate()
      .setTitle('UCBAC Stats - Profile')
      .addMetaTag('viewport', 'width=device-width, initial-scale=1')
      .setXFrameOptionsMode(HtmlService.XFrameOptionsMode.ALLOWALL);
  }

  const t = HtmlService.createTemplateFromFile('Index');
  t.route   = webAppRoute_(e);
  t.siteUrl = String(CONFIG.SITE_URL || '');
  /* The published /exec address, for "Share profile" links. The page cannot
     read it for itself: inside the sandbox frame its own location is a
     googleusercontent address nobody should ever be handed. */
  t.execUrl = String(ScriptApp.getService().getUrl() || '');
  return t
    .evaluate()
    .setTitle('UCBAC Football Scores, Standings & Stats')
    .addMetaTag('viewport', 'width=device-width, initial-scale=1')
    .setXFrameOptionsMode(HtmlService.XFrameOptionsMode.ALLOWALL);
}

/** Public Home markup only. Auth/data services still authorize every request.
 * The portal mounts this owned document locally after login instead of trying
 * to navigate the top Google sandbox after an asynchronous code redemption.
 */
function svcHomeDocument() {
  const t = HtmlService.createTemplateFromFile('Index');
  t.route = '#/';
  t.siteUrl = String(CONFIG.SITE_URL || '');
  t.execUrl = String(ScriptApp.getService().getUrl() || '');
  t.fromPortal = true;
  return t.evaluate().getContent();
}

/**
 * Turn ?p=scores into the hash the app routes on.
 *
 * The Google Site at UCBACstats.com links into this deployment, and it cannot
 * link to a section directly: the page it reaches runs inside Apps Script's
 * sandbox frame, whose document has no access to the hash on the address the
 * reader actually typed. A query parameter does survive - it arrives here in
 * e.parameter - so the SERVER reads the requested page and hands the client an
 * opening route to apply for itself.
 *
 * Everything is whitelisted rather than escaped. The result is dropped into a
 * JavaScript string literal, and the only characters that can reach it are
 * letters, digits, hyphen, underscore and the punctuation this function writes
 * itself, so there is nothing to break out with.
 *
 *   ?p=scores                      -> #/scores
 *   ?p=team&id=TEAM-006            -> #/team/TEAM-006
 *   ?p=stats&side=MEASURE          -> #/stats?side=MEASURE
 *   ?p=home&sec=standings          -> #/?sec=standings
 */
const WEBAPP_PAGES = ['scores', 'teams', 'team', 'player', 'coach', 'game',
                      'stats', 'fantasy', 'allconference', 'standings', 'leaders', 'plays'];
/* These are the Stats page's own filter keys (SDEF in Index.html) plus 'sec',
   which picks a section of Home. Spell them exactly as the page reads them -
   'pos', not 'position' - or the link arrives and silently does nothing. The
   free-text search 'q' is deliberately absent: it is the one filter that
   cannot survive this whitelist intact. */
const WEBAPP_PARAMS = ['sec', 'week', 'season', 'range', 'side', 'scope',
                       'pos', 'team', 'county', 'min', 'sort', 'dir'];

function webAppRoute_(e) {
  const p = (e && e.parameter) || {};
  const clean = function (v) { return String(v || '').replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/g, ''); };

  let page = clean(p.p).toLowerCase();
  if (page === 'all-conference' || page === 'allconf') page = 'allconference';
  if (page === 'home' || WEBAPP_PAGES.indexOf(page) < 0) page = '';

  let hash = '#/' + page;
  const id = clean(p.id);
  if (page && id) hash += '/' + id;

  const qs = [];
  WEBAPP_PARAMS.forEach(function (k) {
    const v = clean(p[k]);
    if (v) qs.push(k + '=' + v);
  });
  if (qs.length) hash += '?' + qs.join('&');

  // '#/' is where the app opens anyway; say nothing rather than route to it.
  return hash === '#/' ? '' : hash;
}

function include_(name) {
  return HtmlService.createHtmlOutputFromFile(name).getContent();
}
